Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the quick onboarding flow — FluxKit really liked the self-serve sign-up. A couple of our maintainers ran into the token limits during a migration test and asked if Redwood can provision a maintainer credit and a short trial extension so we can finish a performance regression run.

Details:

- Org lead: Laura Chen (GitHub: laura-chen)
- Use case: CI benchmark runs + a small hosted demo for project contributors
- Requested credit: $1,500 in platform credits
- Trial extension: 30 days (adds time to finish runs)

I'm attaching a screenshot of the GitHub org membership page and a short note from our maintainer core team for verification.

Could you confirm whether this is eligible for a maintainer/grant-style credit and how we can redeem it? We're happy to provide any extra proof.

Best,

Hi Laura — thanks for the context and the attachment, looks good at a glance.

Quick notes and next steps:
- We typically approve small maintainer allocations for active OSS projects (<= $2,000) on a case-by-case basis.
- I need a short confirmation that FluxKit is listed as an OSS project (link included) and that the credit will be used for CI/benchmarking and contributor-facing demos — you've already mentioned that which is perfect.
- We'll route this through our credit approvals queue. Two things I need from our side to complete: a one-line verification from the project lead (you provided), and an approval from my manager for the amount and the 30-day extension.

I've looped in Vanessa (sales ops) for approval and Soojin (community programs) to record this as a maintainer program issuance. Vanessa / Soojin — can you confirm we can issue $1,500 and add a 30-day extension? If yes I'll prepare the redemption token and send the self-serve link to Laura.
